related_questions.question: How many polio survivors are still alive in the US?

text_blocks.snippet: There are an estimated 300,000 polio survivors living in the United States. Many of them experience post-polio syndrome, a condition that can cause new muscle weakness and pain decades after the initial polio infection, according to the National Organization for Rare Disorders.

While the last case of wild poliovirus in the US was in 1979, and the last case of polio caused by a vaccine was in 2000, the disease continues to affect those who contracted it years ago. Many survivors live with the long-term effects of polio, including post-polio syndrome (PPS), according to the Pennsylvania Immunization Coalition.
Estimates suggest that 25% to 50% of polio survivors may develop PPS. This means that tens of thousands of polio survivors in the US are living with this condition.
